clips.title: The story
paras: From the Tower of Azora, Theocritus uses Glyphs of Azora to watch distant threats. The inscribed stones extend the Eye of Azora's reach, letting him read enemies' thoughts and plans.

Theocritus watches hostile powers from his tower in Elwynn Forest. His crystal relic, the Eye of Azora, lets him see across great distances, but cannot reach into the minds or plans of his adversaries. He places small focuses called Glyphs of Azora on surfaces far away to carry his magic farther. Each glyph anchors his power, letting him read enemy intentions and project his voice across miles to speak with field agents.
